messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: pushed if-then-else and while statements
parts:
For the next release, there is now:

1. Comparison operators: <, >, <=, >=, !=, ==

2. Boolean operators: !, &&, ||

3. If-then-else statements

4. While loops

All of these constructs are directly translated to their
C++ equivalents, and I preserved the C++ syntax and operator
orders and precedences for Stan.

So far, I haven't vectorized or allowed any of the operators
to broadcast, so the comparison and boolean operators only
accept primitive types (int or real).

I still need to add tests for parsing/compilation in
test/gm/parser and add more doc. But it looks like it's
all working.

I still need a good example for while loops! Is there some
kind of iterative algorithm that would make sense to have in
a model where the loop bounds aren't characterized by a simple
integer sequence for (i in L:U) { ... }?

- Bob
